notes: EACH CELL IS 6 × 6 THREADS AT 8 PX.
THE BLENDS ARE WOVEN, NOT MIXED.
blends.reading:
A tartan has six colours from
three threads because the blend
is spatial: at 42 ends per inch
the eye does the mixing, not
the dyer.

provenance.heading: THE COCKBURN COLLECTION, 1810–15  ·  ONE CLOTH, FOUR LABELS
quote: “The Cockburn Collection (1810-15) includes four specimens of the Government tartan labelled;
‘Campbell Argyll’, ‘Grant’, ‘Munro’ and ‘Sutherland’.”   — Scottish Register of Tartans, registration note, SRT 277

comparison.heading: THE SAME SETT, TWICE  ·  EACH NORMALISED TO ITS OWN TOTAL, UNIT FOR UNIT

douglas.body: “The per­fect bal­ance of the weav­ing — ex­actly as many weft shots per inch as there are warp ends, to give a 45-de­gree twill an­gle — is of ut­most im­por­tance in pro­duc­ing a true Tar­tan, as each of the col­or blocks must be squared in its prop­er suc­ces­sion.”
douglas.attribution: — Harriet C. Douglas, Scotch Tartan Setts, Shuttle-Craft Guild, 1949
